canonical_data: per-user memory cubes of extracted memory items held in a graph database and a vector store the operator runs, with users and cubes in a relational store; the agent plugins keep a local file database
current_repo_note: Paper-associated but maintained by a company with a hosted product, a release roughly every one to two weeks, and a multi-platform continuous-integration matrix, so it passes the test that excluded paper harnesses. No published runtime it targets names it as a backend; its integrations run one way from its own adapters, unlike Hindsight and OpenViking, which were confirmed from the runtime side. Plugin directories declare a permissive licence in their manifests with no licence file, and a vendored third-party desktop app carries its own.
strengths: A real service surface of an API, a tool server, a library, and a command line, with a continuous-integration matrix that builds and installs the package on four platforms
Memory cubes give explicit isolation and sharing boundaries across users and agents rather than a single flat store
The local plugin brings the same core to three agent runtimes on-device with a file database and hybrid recall
weaknesses: No runtime it targets names it as a backend; one of them lists eight other memory services and not this one
Licence metadata is inconsistent, with permissive manifests beside no licence file and a badge that links to a different licence text
Defaults are not sovereign: a hosted model provider for every model, telemetry on in the plugin, and every accuracy figure vendor-run
why_it_matters: The most complete open memory service organised around explicit per-user, per-agent memory cubes, shipping both a self-hosted server and on-device plugins, even though the runtimes it targets have not yet reciprocated.
